title: The RAG pipeline
task_statement: Build a retrieval pipeline with named stages and citations that trace each claim to a source. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Search results with citations
components.first_principle: Pass retrieved text as search result blocks so Claude attaches a source and title to each cited claim.
steps: Retrieve candidate chunks from your index before the model call.
Wrap each chunk in a search_result block with a source and a title.
Set citations to enabled on every search result in the request.
Claude writes the answer and attaches citation blocks to the cited text.
Each citation names a search_result_index and a block range.
Check the citations array before you show the answer to a user. (Inference)
pros: Citations link each claim to a source and title that you supply.
The cited_text field does not count toward output tokens.
Search results work in tool results and in top-level user message content.
cons: Citations and structured outputs cannot combine in one request.
All search results in one request must use the same citations setting.
Search result content holds text blocks only, with no images.
use_when: Answers must name the source document for each claim.
Your app retrieves text at runtime from a knowledge base.
The retrieved text is ready before the model call starts.
do_not_use_when: The output must follow a strict JSON schema, because citations conflict with structured outputs.
The source content is image only, because search results hold text.
The answer needs no source attribution.

constraints.choice: Expect a slight input token increase when citations are enabled.
constraints.combination: Put cache_control on the search result blocks to reuse the source text.

constraints.choice: Use a source value that your access policy can audit, such as a URL or an internal identifier.
constraints.combination: Use the same source value for every chunk from one document. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Pass several search results in one request, each with its own title.
constraints.combination: Limit the number of results to the ones the answer needs. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Log the search_result_index and block indices for each citation.
constraints.combination: Alert when a grounded answer has an empty citations array. (Inference)

native_services.text: Not in source. The search results page names no native platform service.

components.exam_tie: D3.5. Expect a scenario where answers need source names. The credited answer passes retrieved text as search results with citations enabled. (Inference)
components.trap: A prompt that asks the model to list sources in plain text looks simple. The names are not tied to retrieved blocks, so you cannot check them. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Return retrieved text as search result blocks when the answer needs verifiable source attribution.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario requires cited claims, choose search result blocks with citations enabled.

components.name: Embeddings and reranking models
components.first_principle: Convert text to vectors for similarity search, then reorder a short list with a reranker.
steps: Embed each document chunk with input_type set to document.
Embed the user query with input_type set to query.
Run a nearest neighbor search over the stored vectors.
Send the top candidates and the query to a reranker.
Keep the highest ranked passages for the model context.
pros: Embeddings measure semantic similarity between query and document text.
Voyage AI offers general, multilingual, code, legal, and finance models.
Rerankers return documents ranked by relevance to the query.
cons: Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model, so you add a second vendor.
Vectors must be embedded again when the embedding model changes. (Inference)
A reranker adds a second model call and extra latency. (Inference)
use_when: The corpus needs a domain model, such as a legal or code model.
The answer is in the candidate list, but the ranking is weak. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: Queries contain only exact codes or identifiers, where keyword match fits better. (Inference)
Your procurement policy allows no second vendor. (Inference)
The whole corpus fits in the context window without a pipeline. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep each input within the model context length, such as 32,000 tokens for voyage-4 or 16,000 for voyage-law-2.
constraints.combination: Set enable_auto_chunking to true with voyage-context-4 to accept up to 120,000 tokens.

constraints.choice: Use voyage-4-lite when latency and cost bind.
constraints.combination: Use int8 or binary output to cut vector storage by 4x or 32x.

constraints.choice: Use an Atlas model API key scoped to a geography, which uses that geography endpoint.
Request a smaller output dimension, such as 256 or 512, to shrink vectors.
constraints.combination: Truncate stored vectors to the leading dimensions and normalize them again.

constraints.choice: Set input_type on every retrieval embedding call.
constraints.combination: Do not omit input_type or set it to None.

native_services.text: Not in source. Voyage AI models also appear on AWS Marketplace, which is a vendor channel, not a native service.

components.exam_tie: D3.5. Expect a scenario with a retrieval gap. The credited answer names the stage that fails and changes only that stage. (Inference)
components.trap: An Anthropic embedding model looks like the default choice. Anthropic does not offer one, so the design needs an embeddings vendor.
components.decision_rule: Add a reranker when the answer appears in the candidates but ranks low. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the answer is absent from the candidates, fix retrieval before you add a reranker. (Inference)

components.name: Chunk granularity for citations
components.first_principle: Choose the document type whose chunk boundaries match the citation granularity you need.

nodes.label: Your chunker at headings and tables

steps: Split the source at headings, sections, and table boundaries. (Inference)
Send each chunk as a plain text document when sentence citations are enough.
Send each chunk as custom content when you need your own block boundaries.
Plain text documents chunk into sentences and cite character indices.
Custom content documents keep your blocks and cite block indices.
Confirm that each table stays in one chunk before you index it. (Inference)
pros: Plain text documents need no custom block logic.
Custom content gives finer control for lists and transcripts.
Citations keep source and title for each document.
cons: Automatic sentence chunking ignores your heading and table boundaries. (Inference)
Custom content requires you to define each block boundary.
A claim split across two blocks produces a wider citation range. (Inference)
use_when: Each retrieved chunk is a separate document with its own source.
Citations must point to specific sentences in long passages.
Lists or transcripts need citations at block level.
do_not_use_when: The output must follow a strict JSON schema, because citations conflict with structured outputs.
Whole documents fit in context and no chunk boundary is needed. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use plain text documents for simple prose with the least preparation.
Cited text does not count toward output tokens.
constraints.combination: Expect a small input token increase for chunking and citation prompts.

constraints.choice: Use custom content for lists, transcripts, and special layouts.
constraints.combination: Keep each block small enough to cite on its own. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep the source and title on each document for audit.

native_services.text: Not in source. The citations page names no native platform service for chunking.

components.exam_tie: D3.5. Expect a scenario with split tables or lists in citations. The credited answer changes the chunk boundary, not the citation setting. (Inference)
components.trap: Plain text documents look simpler, but automatic sentence chunking ignores table boundaries. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use custom content when your own chunk boundaries must become the citation boundaries.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names split tables, fix the chunker before you change citation settings. (Inference)

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Answer needs source attribution?} -->|No| X[Plain prompt with no citations]
  A -->|Yes| B{Output must match a strict JSON schema?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Separate citation step from schema step]
  B -->|No| D{Retrieved text split across blocks?}
  D -->|Yes| E[Re-chunk at document structure]
  D -->|No| F[Search result blocks with citations enabled]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  Q[Query] --> E[Embed with input_type query]
  E --> N[Nearest neighbor search]
  N --> R[Rerank top candidates]
  R --> S[Search result blocks]
  S --> C[Citations enabled]
  C --> A[Answer with cited spans]
